free_text_notes.physician_note: 52-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, admitted 5/7 with small right cerebellar infarct. MRI confirmed small infarct; no hemorrhagic conversion. 5/11 10:00: BP 214/118 this morning despite oral agents; not at discharge threshold.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Slept well overnight. Voiding without difficulty. 5/10 15:00: Lisinopril changed from 10 mg daily to 20 mg daily this morning. Reviewed with patient and daughter at 15:00; teach-back correct. The patient had a brief episode of a urinary tract infection earlier this year. It was treated with a short course of antibiotics and fully resolved. A screening blood test for thyroid function was added on day 2 as part of a routine check. The result came back normal. No clinical action is required.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: CM following for discharge planning. Discharge paperwork still waiting on the summary.
